request.deadline: Three-month liquidity deployment after enactment with monthly reporting; other delivery timing not fully stated in document.
deliverables: Shared BTC reserve architecture with transparent safety mechanisms and reserve-ratio rules
Composable Cardano-native FIRE and ICE assets
Open-source SDKs and adapters for wallets, DEXs, and DeFi protocols
Always-on public dashboards for reserve ratio, asset supply, liquidity health, fee flows, and deployment status
Monthly governance reports and reporting standards
Independent security review, audit, and economic modeling
Staged treasury-supported launch liquidity split approximately USD 800,000 FIRE-side and USD 200,000 ICE-side
Legal, compliance, disclosures, treasury reporting, risk documentation, and launch-readiness review
Ecosystem education, DRep communications, partner activation, and launch coordination
request.recipient: Intersect is proposed as interim fund administrator, subject to confirmation and final agreement; Sundial remains accountable for deployment and delivery with Charms as technical partner.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Alchemy, a Cardano-native Bitcoin treasury protocol and BTCfi infrastructure layer with reserve architecture, FIRE/ICE assets, dashboards, adapters, reporting, audits, legal/compliance work, go-to-market execution, and staged launch liquidity.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 10,000,000 ada, using an approximate USD 0.20 per ada reference rate for a planning budget of approximately USD 2.0 million split into two approximately USD 1.0 million pools.

Pool 1 is intended for protocol infrastructure and staged launch liquidity, kept separate from operating spend, deployed over three months, and designed to return launch-liquidity profits, yield, and returns to the Cardano Treasury quarterly.

Pool 2 funds delivery, audit, integrations, dashboards, governance reporting, legal/compliance work, and go-to-market execution with itemized planning allocations totaling approximately USD 1.0 million.

Alchemy proposes a shared BTC reserve backing FIRE and ICE, with a reserve-ratio formula, an initial 5.0x target reserve ratio, and safety zones above 4.0x, between 2.0x and 4.0x, and below 2.0x that constrain minting, redemption, and risky activity.

FIRE is described as a volatility-absorbing residual BTC reserve claim with upside and first-loss downside, while ICE is described as lower-volatility USD-denominated BTC-backed exposure with growth potential.

The proposal claims Cardano lacks a serious production BTCfi infrastructure layer and that without one Bitcoin-backed structured exposure will continue consolidating on other chains and off-chain markets.

The proposal cites Strategy, Strive, Apyx, Saturn, Pendle, and related markets as evidence that demand for Bitcoin-backed structured exposure is real and growing, with some linked external references for Strategy and governance context.

The proposal identifies Charms protocol-layer, bridge, oracle, asset-accounting, BTC volatility, novel asset, delivery, and adoption risks, and proposes mitigations including independent review, economic modeling, staged deployment, dashboards, pause rules, legal work, disclosures, milestone gating, and administrator oversight.
The proposal states there will be no DRep funds or personal compensation to Sundial or Charms principals and includes a rollover commitment if external investment funds Alchemy development.

The proposal states it is self-contained, denominated in ada, designed to comply with the current Cardano Constitution and prevailing Net Change Limit, and includes administrator custody expectations with administrator-held ada delegated to auto-abstain.

summary: The document requests 10,000,000 ada for Alchemy by Sundial x Charms, describing a two-pool budget for BTCfi protocol infrastructure, staged launch liquidity, FIRE/ICE assets, audits, integrations, dashboards, reporting, legal/compliance, and go-to-market work. It provides substantial internal detail on mechanics, budget categories, staged liquidity, and claimed safeguards, while several major market, adoption, compliance, and feasibility claims remain proposer-asserted or externally checkable rather than proven within the document.
